ops.title: Workflow agents in daemonkit die to the 180s stall detector — how to brief around it
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01/02, daemonkit P4.1 Lane D. One agent, 352k tokens, 69 tool calls, 95
minutes, ZERO files written. Six attempts, all killed by the harness no-progress detector at 180s.

Read from the six transcripts, the failure had three distinct causes:

1. **A foreground long command with no incremental output.** Attempt 1 ended on
   `./scripts/test.sh -race -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. The suite takes minutes (the root
   package alone is 19-72s depending on load), and `| tail` buffers everything, so the harness saw
   zero progress and killed it mid-run. Any full-suite run in this repo exceeds 180s. Piping
   through `tail`/`head` guarantees the kill.

2. **Recon that never converts to writing.** Attempts 1 and 2 spent 49 and 20 tool calls on
   `cat -n` of whole files (serve.go, cmd.go, session.go, owned.go, childside_test.go). The repo
   has ccx precisely to avoid this. Budget went to reading; nothing was built.

3. **A prompt so large the model thought past the deadline before its first tool call.** Attempts
   3-6 each produced a transcript of exactly 46,042 bytes — the prompt, and nothing else. Zero tool
   calls in 180 seconds. The brief told the agent to read four sections of a 915-line design plus
   AGENTS.md (40KB), CLAUDE.md (17KB), and STYLEGUIDE.md before writing anything.

What to do instead, all three confirmed on the re-dispatch:

- **Background every long command and poll in separate tool calls.**
  `cmd > /tmp/log 2>&1 &`, then `sleep 20; tail -5 /tmp/log` as its own call. Each poll is
  progress, so the detector never fires.
- **Test one package while iterating** (`scripts/test.sh -race -count=1 .`), full `./...` only at
  the end, backgrounded.
- **Inline the contract; do not send the agent to read it.** Extract the 40 relevant design lines
  into the prompt. A stage that needs a 900-line document read first is a stage that is too big.
- **Split the lane.** Four small sequential stages, each with a narrow scope and its own
  build+vet+one-package-test gate, beat one agent holding the whole surface.
- **Tell the agent to act within its first minute.** An early cheap tool call resets the clock.

Prior art in the same phase: the Lane B build agent also stalled once (805s) and recovered on
retry 1 — the detector is not rare, and an agent that survives it is not evidence the brief was
sized right. See [[a-design-that-overflowed-one-output-block]] for the sibling failure mode where
the deliverable, not the agent, was the thing that got truncated.
ops.when: Before dispatching a Workflow or subagent that will build, test, or gate anything in daemonkit
